raw_response:
**My reasoning:**

I've farmed this land since I was a teenager helping my father. In Quzhou, there's really only one system that makes sense: winter wheat in autumn, then summer corn on the same fields. Everyone here does it. The purchasing station buys my wheat at the government support price, and corn merchants come to the village in autumn — I don't need to travel. My 12 mu is flat, the well reaches water, and I know how this soil behaves.

I'll plant 11 mu in the wheat-corn rotation. I keep 1 mu close to the house for vegetables — garlic, cabbage, and some beans — but that's for eating, not planning.

For wheat, I'll buy improved seed from the county seed station — the variety my brother-in-law used last year (Shimai 15 type). Hybrid is for corn. I'll spread compound fertilizer as base and come back with urea in early spring when wheat starts jointing. I water three times: once before winter freeze, once at jointing, once at grain fill. I spray herbicide in winter and go out again in May when aphids show up.

For corn, I go straight in after wheat harvest with no tillage — no time between June wheat cut and corn planting. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958, reliable. Fertilizer heavier on nitrogen. If July rains are enough I won't irrigate at all, but usually I pump once in August when ears are filling.

I rotary till before wheat each October to bury the corn stalks.
